name: ddate
desc: Converts boring normal dates to fun Discordian Date
why: Converts dates to the Discordian calendar; a small oddity with real calendar-system charm.

brief.what_it_is: ddate is a small C command-line program that converts Gregorian dates to the Discordian calendar, the 'POEE' calendar named in the README. It is a perpetual converter. The README describes the calendar's structure (five seasons of 73 days, five weekday names, apostle and seasonal holydays, and an occasional Saint Tib's Day) and gives build steps, but it does not show example input or output. The source is a single ddate.c file built with CMake.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says this is the ddate source taken from util-linux 2.20, kept here because util-linux no longer builds ddate by default and the Arch Linux package maintainer seemed happy to drop it. It is also available from the AUR.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives the calendar layout rather than the algorithm: five seasons (Chaos, Discord, Confusion, Bureaucracy, The Aftermath), each with 73 days, weekdays named Sweetmorn, Boomtime, Pungenday, Prickle-Prickle and Setting Orange, and holydays on the 5th day (apostle holydays) and 50th day (season holydays) of each season. Saint Tib's Day is inserted once every four years between the 59th and 60th days of Chaos. The README includes a large year table mapping Gregorian dates to Discordian dates, but it does not explain how the conversion is computed.

commands_seen.context: Creates a build directory before compiling, as the first step of the README's BUILDING section.
Configures the build with CMake from the parent directory, which holds CMakeLists.txt.
Installs the built ddate binary, per the README's build steps.

brief.install_notes: Build with CMake: mkdir build, cd build, cmake .., make, make install. The README does not mention any runtime, account, or configuration. It is also available from the AUR for Arch users. The README does not say whether a Homebrew formula is provided.
brief.standout: It is a tiny, single-purpose C program that carries a whole fictional calendar system, complete with a sacred document, weekday names, and a leap-day rule modelled on the Gregorian one ('1 + 4 = 5'). The README's own framing of the 'Sacred Document of the Frogs' poem and its wholesale re-hosting of a util-linux tool give it a particular charm.
brief.status: Unknown in detail. The repository has 41 commits, 113 stars and 35 forks. The README says the code is exactly the util-linux 2.20 version, so it is effectively frozen rather than actively developed. I could not see a last commit date or release date in the fetched page.
brief.caveats: The README does not show how to invoke ddate, what input it accepts, or what its output looks like, and I did not fetch the ddate.1 manual page or README.org. Build requires CMake and a C compiler. The README warns that util-linux no longer builds ddate by default. No license was visible in the fetched text.
quotes: PERPETUAL DATE CONVERTER FROM GREGORIAN TO POEE CALENDAR
73 Days hath Chaos, Discord, Confusion, Bureaucracy, and Aftermath
This is exactly the same ddate version that can be found in the util-linux 2.20 release.
